title: Onramp Guidelines and Retirement Safeguards for Visual Primitives
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Establish a lightweight contributor onramp plus a controlled retirement (component retirement) pattern for tokens and visual primitives (buttons, tables, charts) that balances speed of contribution with long-term maintainability and predictable migration for product teams.
problem_statement: Design contributions are fast but inconsistent: new tokens and component variants are added without migration paths, ownership, or clear impact on accessibility and runtime costs. This leads to duplication, regression risk, and higher maintenance debt for the design system and engineering runtime.
goals: 1) Provide a minimal, tested checklist for new contributions. 2) Define a predictable retirement path for deprecated tokens/components with automated migration support where possible. 3) Reduce accidental duplication and clarify ownership and rollback processes.
non_goals: This ticket does not redesign existing tokens or migrate existing components; it defines the process and tooling to be used in future changes.
proposed_solution: 1) Contributor Onramp: a 5-step checklist (design brief + Figma token file update + accessibility audit + unit/regression tests + PR template). 2) Retirement Safeguards: retirement RFC with 90-day window, automated codemod support for common token name changes, feature-flagged rollouts for UI changes. 3) Ownership Matrix: assign owners by primitive (tokens, buttons, tables, charts) and require owner sign-off for breaking or deprecating changes.
acceptance_criteria: A clear contributor checklist doc exists in Confluence and is linked from the Design Registry
A retirement RFC template added to the RFC repo with required fields: motivation, migration plan, fallback, metrics
Codemod proof-of-concept that renames a simple token and updates 3 example repos
Design owner assignments published and visible in the registry
A staged rollout playbook documented for runtime and console changes
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Draft checklist + RFC template + owner nominations. Phase 2 (3 weeks): Pilot with two component deprecations (secondary button variant and legacy small table). Phase 3 (2 weeks): Ship codemod PoC and integrate checklist into PR templates. Phase 4: Iterate on feedback and finalize policy.
risks_and_mitigation: High friction for contributors if the checklist is overly prescriptive — mitigate by keeping checklist as 'must-have' vs 'nice-to-have' sections
Incomplete codemod coverage could leave teams with broken styles — mitigate by starting with token renames only and requiring manual QA on complex cases
Owners unavailable for sign-off causing blockers — mitigate by adding secondary owners and an escalation path to Design Leads
implementation_notes: Keep checklist itself as a living doc; integrate the minimal checklist into the component template in the Design Registry. Work with SDK owners to expose a token mapping endpoint to support codemod verification in CI. Prototype codemod using jscodeshift for React + token-name mapping exported from Figma tokens JSON.
measurement: Track number of contributions that include checklist sign-off, count of deprecations that followed the RFC process, and number of migration failures reported. Target: 90% checklist compliance for new component submissions within 60 days of rollout.

notes: This policy aims to reduce long tail maintenance while preserving rapid iteration. Avoid heavy-handed enforcement at launch: prefer education and lightweight CI checks before requiring hard blocks. Revisit after the pilot and measure adoption metrics.
